analysis.title: Hedge Fund CIO: "A Storm Of Coming Problems Will Force People To Argue Over Whether To Shut AI Off, If That's Even Possible"
key_insights: Oct 27-28 FOMC minutes said almost all participants judged further rate hikes would likely be appropriate to return inflation to 2%. The S&P 500 closed Friday 10.8% below its Oct 28 level and the Nasdaq 100 was 16% lower.

Fed Governor Waller said inflation is heading in the wrong direction and spreading, and pressed for a 50bp hike in December. Goolsbee cited multiple months of borderline disturbingly high inflation, and Cook warned of falling behind the curve.
Sparks argues AI is the first existential-risk technology that cannot be contained, since anyone can access it, unlike nuclear weapons that require enriched uranium.

Sparks's thesis is that AI can find every weakness in legal, financial and software systems, and that walls can only be rebuilt by AI through recursive self-improvement, which makes it impossible to understand or turn off.
Sparks expects the next 1-3 years to go badly as old systems are hit by a godlike one, with hysteria, chaos and disruption.
Sparks says stocks are 40-50% too high on their own merits, with earnings 30% above the 50-year trend line, driven by a leveraged circular funding system, and the Fed is now tightening.
Sparks expects a future bear market when society fights over whether to turn AI off, and says data center moratorium fights are minor compared to that.
Sparks's portfolio advice is to own Treasuries in the 3-5 year sector and to adopt a survival mindset.
Anecdote: leveraged Nvidia longs were hurt when the stock rose after a blowout earnings report on Tuesday but lost 23% on the week by Friday's close.
Peters cites the February 2018 collapse of inverse VIX products, which lost 96% in an afternoon with no specific catalyst, as an example of crowded positioning being flushed.

market_movers.rationale: Stock rose after hours on a blowout earnings report Tuesday but lost 23% on the week by Friday's close, punishing leveraged longs.

sector_views.rationale: Sparks says the entire market is levered to the AI trade, earnings are in a bubble, and AI-related problems will drive a bear market.
Sparks recommends owning Treasuries at threes to fives as the defensive holding.

Sparks says S&P earnings are 30% above the 50-year trend line, a level he attributes to a leveraged circular money system.
